description: Georgia-only rules checked against the Official Code and the Department of Driver Services teen pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless appropriate signs designate another limit, the maximum in a Georgia urban or residential district is
questions.explanation: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-181 sets 30 mph in any urban or residential district unless otherwise designated by appropriate signs.

questions.q: Unless signs designate otherwise, the maximum on an unpaved Georgia county road is
questions.explanation: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-181 sets 35 mph on an unpaved county road unless designated otherwise by appropriate signs.

questions.q: A 70 mph limit on a Georgia interstate is lawful when
options: The road is an interstate, with or without a speed sign
It is outside a city only
It is 70 for cars and 55 for every other vehicle
questions.explanation: Section 40-6-181 sets 70 mph on an interstate both outside and inside an urbanized area of 50,000 or more, provided appropriate signs designate that limit. The same sign requirement applies to 65 mph on a physically divided state highway without full access control.

questions.q: Where O.C.G.A. § 40-6-181 does not set one of the signed higher limits, the maximum is
questions.explanation: The section sets 55 mph in other locations. Those maximums may be altered under sections 40-6-182, 40-6-183, and 40-6-188. The section does not set one statewide school-zone number.

questions.q: Georgia's per se alcohol rule is an alcohol concentration of 0.08 grams or more
options: Only if a breath test is taken at the roadside
At any time within three hours after driving
questions.explanation: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391(a)(5). The section also prohibits driving under the influence of alcohol to the extent it is less safe, even below that number. At any time within three hours after driving, from alcohol consumed before the driving ended.

questions.q: A person under 21 may not drive in Georgia with an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391(k) uses 0.02 grams or more within three hours after driving, from alcohol consumed before the driving ended.

questions.q: Georgia assesses reckless driving
questions.explanation: O.C.G.A. § 40-5-57(c) assesses 4 points for reckless driving and 6 points for aggressive driving.

questions.q: The Georgia commissioner suspends a license at
questions.explanation: The 24 months are measured from the dates of the arrests for which convictions were obtained. At the end of the suspension, the point count is reduced to zero. 15 or more points in any consecutive 24-month period.

questions.q: Too fast for conditions is assessed
questions.explanation: The O.C.G.A. § 40-5-57 schedule lists too fast for conditions as 0 points. Other moving violations that are not speed-limit violations are 3 points unless the schedule gives them a different number.

questions.q: A Georgia Class D license holder may not drive between
options: 11 p.m. and 5 a.m., with a work exception
Midnight and 5 a.m., with no exceptions
questions.explanation: The Georgia Department of Driver Services says a Class D holder may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m., with no exceptions. The restriction follows the license class, not only the driver's age.

questions.q: During the first six months of a Georgia Class D license, the only passengers allowed are
options: Any passenger if it is daylight
questions.explanation: DDS: first six months, only immediate family. Second six months, only one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family. After one year, only three passengers under 21 who are not immediate family.

questions.q: Joshua's Law requires a 16-year-old applying for a Georgia Class D license to have held a learner's permit for
questions.explanation: DDS says all teens must hold a learner's permit for 1 year and 1 day before a Class D license. A 16-year-old must also complete an approved driver-education method.

questions.q: One approved Joshua's Law method for a 16-year-old is 30 hours of classroom instruction, 6 hours behind the wheel at a certified school, and
options: 40 hours with a parent, 6 at night
questions.explanation: That is Method 1 on the DDS Joshua's Law page. Method 2 uses 40 hours of parent-taught behind-the-wheel training instead of the school's 6 hours behind the wheel. A parent or guardian must be present at DDS to attest to the training. 40 hours of supervised driving with a parent or guardian, including 6 at night.

questions.q: After the first year of a Georgia Class D license, passengers under 21 who are not immediate family are limited to
questions.explanation: DDS states that limit for the period after one year from issuance. The first six months are immediate family only, and the second six months allow one non-family passenger under 21.

questions.q: Georgia's 0.02 rule applies to
options: Drivers over 21 in a school zone
questions.explanation: O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391(k) is the under-21 rule. The 0.08 rule in subsection (a)(5) is the general per se rule. This file does not state a separate commercial 0.04 number because that number is not in the subsection used here.

questions.q: In Georgia, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Georgia issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Georgia car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: Section 2: Obtaining a License, Permit, or ID | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: In Georgia, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Georgia requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 12 months.

provenance.manual: Section 2: Obtaining a License, Permit, or ID | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Georgia complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Georgia requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Section 2: Obtaining a License, Permit, or ID | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: Of a Georgia teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Georgia requires at least 6 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Georgia: 6 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Section 2: Obtaining a License, Permit, or ID | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: In Georgia, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Georgia, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Section 2: Obtaining a License, Permit, or ID | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Georgia not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Georgia restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Georgia new drivers: off the road Midnight to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: How do I get a Class D license \| Georgia DDS

questions.q: In Georgia, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Georgia drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: Section 1 Continued | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: How many questions are on the Georgia car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Georgia car knowledge test has 40 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Georgia car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 75% to pass the Georgia car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Georgia, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Georgia, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Georgia, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: Section 2 Continued | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: In Georgia, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Georgia brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Georgia, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

provenance.manual: Section 10: Losing Your Driving Privileges | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Georgia?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Georgia can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Georgia rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

provenance.manual: Georgia Drivers Manual | Department of Driver Services

questions.q: Which best describes Georgia's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Georgia: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Chapter 2: Traffic Laws & Safe Driving | Georgia Department of Driver Services

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Georgia?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Georgia, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Georgia left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

provenance.manual: Georgia Drivers Manual | Department of Driver Services

questions.q: How is Georgia's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Georgia seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Georgia Drivers Manual | Department of Driver Services

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Georgia?
questions.explanation: Georgia requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Georgia: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is Georgia's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Georgia requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under Georgia's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Georgia can suspend an adult's license at 15 points in 24 months.

provenance.manual: Points and Points Reduction | Georgia Department of Driver Services
